groups.sentence: Course policies are educational, not punitive, and misuse is a chance to learn and adapt.
Instructors encourage students to ask for extensions when struggling, to reduce pressures that lead to cheating.
Conduct and integrity processes are educational and supportive, so most first reports lead to educational outcomes, reminders or reflection rather than formal charges.
Instructors talk with the student in an open, supportive, education-focused way, explaining the concern and assuming good faith.
Instructors treat suspected or confirmed AI misuse, especially first offenses, as a teachable moment rather than only discipline.
Instructors offer the student a chance to revise, rewrite, redo or resubmit the work after suspected misuse.
Instructors respond to violations with fair, educative, remedial sanctions and mild intervention for initial occurrences.
Instructors can establish progressive remedial steps giving students prevention, clarification and corrective intervention before formal disciplinary action.
The university develops and deploys educational modules to help students who commit violations.
Instructors adopt a teaching-oriented, proactive rather than punitive approach to AI before any misuse occurs.
Educators' primary work is to support students' development and foster exploration rather than to surveil, discipline or punish them.
The university avoids highly restrictive and punitive rules on generative AI use.
